# CS-04 — Sorting 20 artifacts into PMBOK 7 domains

!!! info "Case card"
    **Difficulty:** Beginner (CS-01..CS-20) ·
    **Level:** L1 — Single-concept drill ·
    **Domain:** D1 · **Seed project:** standalone

## Learning objectives

1. Map concrete artifacts to PMBOK 7's domain structure.
2. Recognize that artifact purpose, not format, determines domain.

## Project context

You are given 20 artifact names collected from real CS and data-science projects — from charters and burndown charts to model cards and rollback plans.

## Problem statement

Assign each artifact to its primary PMBOK 7 performance domain and flag any artifact that legitimately belongs to two.

## Constraints and available information

- One primary domain per artifact; secondary allowed with a one-line justification.
- Domain names must match PMBOK 7's eight performance domains.

## Student tasks

1. Sort all 20 artifacts into the eight domains.
2. Identify the three artifacts most often mis-sorted and explain the confusion.
3. Name one artifact your team has never seen and what domain it would serve.

## Expected deliverables

- Artifact-to-domain table.
- Short note on the three confusion pairs.

## Discussion questions

1. Why does PMBOK 7 organize by domains rather than process groups?
1. Which domain has the weakest artifact evidence in student projects, and why?

## How you will be graded

Sorting accuracy (60%); confusion-pair explanations show the underlying principle (30%); original artifact suggestion is coherent (10%).

## Where this case appears

- Anchored in [Lecture 03](../lectures/L03-03-pmbok7-principles-domains.md).
- Suggested use: in-class.
